getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.summary: From sign-in to your first CDS consult the same day.
getting-started.tip: Recommended order: Dashboard → owner + pet → GUIAA Diagnosis. CDS organizes the case; you define the diagnosis and plan.
body: GUIAA is a clinical platform for licensed veterinarians. The core is a structured consult with CDS (Clinical Decision Support): it helps you capture and organize the case by species — it does not replace your professional judgment.
Beyond diagnosis you can run schedule, records, inventory, sales, and reports depending on your plan. Start with a real or practice patient and complete one consult end to end.
steps: Sign in with your verified veterinary account.
Check the Dashboard: today’s appointments, alerts, and quick actions.
Create an owner and pet under Owners & pets.
Open GUIAA Diagnosis, pick the correct species, and complete the consult.
Save the case and confirm it in History or on the patient chart.
Use Ctrl+K (⌘K on Mac) if you can’t find a module.

cds.title: What CDS is (L4 and L5)
cds.summary: Clinical decision support: what it means, what it does, and what it does not do.
cds.tip: CDS structures case reasoning. L4 organizes hypotheses; L5 supports the plan. You validate, adjust, and take clinical responsibility for the outcome.
body: CDS means Clinical Decision Support. In GUIAA it is the workflow that accompanies you during the consult so information stays complete, ordered, and traceable — chief complaint, history, exam, findings, hypotheses, and plan.

It is not an automatic diagnosis and not a closed order. It does not replace examination, complementary tests, or your judgment. If something does not match the patient in front of you, your criterion prevails.
L4 focuses on diagnostic reasoning: helping organize signs and history into reviewable differentials. L5 moves toward therapeutic and follow-up guidance documented from what you captured.
Use CDS when you want a complete, reproducible consult. In emergencies on Premium, Expert Mode lets you describe the case first and then land in the clinical structure.
steps: Open a new consult and select species and patient.
Complete chief complaint, signs, and physical exam with clinical honesty (don’t leave critical gaps).
Move to the CDS block: review L4 hypotheses and adjust them to your impression.
If applicable, document plan and follow-up in L5 according to your decision.
Save and confirm the case appears in History and on the chart.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.summary: Day overview: appointments, clinical activity, and shortcuts into the CDS flow.
dashboard.tip: Jump to consults, schedule, or membership from here. Check stock and appointment alerts before you see patients.
body: The Dashboard concentrates daily operations and recent clinical activity. Use it as an entry board, not as the chart: case detail lives in Diagnosis, History, and the patient record.
steps: Review today’s appointments and your plan / consult quota.
Use “New consult” or quick owner/pet registration.
Review recent activity to reopen a case or follow up.
Open inventory or schedule alerts from the side menu when shown.

diagnosis.title: GUIAA Diagnosis
diagnosis.summary: Structured clinical consult with CDS support — under your judgment.
diagnosis.tip: Species → history → exam → CDS (hypotheses/plan) → save. You can export a PDF at the end.
body: This module is the clinical core of GUIAA. Forms change by species so you don’t miss relevant findings in dogs, cats, or non-conventional species.
CDS support organizes reasoning; you decide diagnosis, differentials, treatment, and what to tell the owner. The consult stays linked to the patient for the next visit.
steps: Select or create the pet and confirm the correct species.
Complete chief complaint, signs, and physical exam.
Use the CDS flow to structure hypotheses (L4) and plan (L5) based on your reading of the case.
Save the consult; it appears in History and on the patient chart.
Export PDF if you need to deliver or archive the summary.
On Premium, Expert Mode lets you describe the case first (useful in emergencies).

clients.title: Owners & pets
clients.summary: Owner and patient records in one place.
clients.tip: Register the owner first, then add pets. Open the chart for history, problems, and timeline.
body: This is where tutor and patient identity live. A solid record prevents orphan consults and lets you resume history, allergies, and open problems on the next visit.
steps: Tap “New record” to create owner + pet together.
Search by name, phone, or pet in the top bar.
Open the file and tap “Open chart” for the full clinical chart.
Edit allergies, vaccines, surgeries, and problems; the timeline shows consults and lab.
Start a consult or lab interpretation from the patient.

agenda.title: Schedule
agenda.summary: Weekly appointments, statuses, and online requests.
agenda.tip: Create appointments, update status, and share the portal link so owners can request slots.
body: The schedule connects clinic operations with clinical care. Keep statuses current so the team knows who is arriving and who was already seen.
steps: Move through the week with arrows or jump to “Today”.
Tap “New appointment” and choose patient, time, and notes.
Update status: scheduled, confirmed, completed, and so on.
Copy the portal link for owner requests.
Review pending requests (menu badge) and accept or decline them.

inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.tip: Add products with unit and minimum stock. Sales can deduct inventory.
body: Keep medicines and supplies with alert thresholds so you don’t discover shortages mid-consult. Link stock to sales when you charge clinic products.
steps: Add a product (medicine, supply, or service).
Set quantity, unit, and low-stock threshold.
Review the summary: product totals and alerts.
Correct stock with movements when merchandise arrives.

billing.title: Billing / Sales
billing.summary: Clinical receipts linked to owner, patient, and inventory (not tax invoicing).
billing.tip: Create a sale, add product or service lines, and save the receipt.
body: Use this to document clinic charges tied to the case. It does not issue formal tax invoices; it is GUIAA’s operational receipt.
steps: Tap “New sale” and select owner/patient if applicable.
Add inventory products or free-form concepts.
Set payment method and receipt notes.
Save: the receipt appears in the list and may affect stock.

reports.title: Reports
reports.tip: Choose 7, 30, or 90 days to see consults, revenue, and top products.
body: Use reports to see CDS consult volume, sales activity, and inventory. It is a management board, not a formal accounting close.
steps: Select the period at the top.
Review consult, sales, and inventory KPIs.
Identify top products and trends.
Export CSV if you need the numbers in Excel.

history.title: Consult history
history.summary: Past CDS consults, with filters and a link to the chart.
history.tip: Filter by status, search by patient, reopen a consult, or jump to the pet chart.
body: History is your clinical work archive. Use it for follow-up, case continuity, and internal documentation review.
steps: Use status filters (all, draft, completed…).
Search by pet or owner name.
Open a consult to see the species form and CDS detail.
If the consult has a linked patient, use “Chart” for the clinical record.
Start a new consult from the top button when needed.

lab.title: Imaging / laboratory
lab.summary: Interpret studies and save clinical notes linked to the patient.
lab.tip: Pick patient, study type, and paste or describe findings. You can add PDF context.
body: Complement the CDS consult with lab or imaging interpretations. The note stays on the patient so reviews keep clinical thread.
steps: Select or search the patient.
Set the study type (lab, imaging, etc.).
Paste result text or write your clinical interpretation.
Save: it appears in the module interpretation history.

tools.title: Clinical tools
tools.summary: Dose calculator and external references for consult support.
tools.tip: Enter weight and mg/kg dose; add concentration if you need volume or units to administer.
body: These are calculation and reference aids. Always confirm with the product insert, real weight, and patient context before prescribing.
steps: Open Tools from the clinical menu.
Enter weight (kg) and dose (mg/kg).
Choose presentation and concentration if applicable.
Review the result and confirm with the insert before administration.

settings.title: Settings
settings.summary: Clinic data, team, appointment portal, and password.
settings.tip: Only owner/admin edit the clinic. Invite the team by email with the right role.
body: Configure your clinic identity and who can operate each area. The appointment portal lets owners request times without entering the clinical panel.
steps: Update clinic name and time zone.
Copy the owner appointment portal link.
Invite receptionists, veterinarians, or admins by email.
Manage pending members and change your account password.
From here you can also reopen the welcome tour.

membership.title: Membership
membership.summary: Plans, consult quota, and practice modules.
membership.tip: Compare Basic, Professional, and Premium. Trial limits consults; activate a plan to continue.
body: Your plan defines how many CDS consults you can document and which operational modules you get (inventory, sales, reports, lab, Expert Mode, and more).
steps: Review your current plan and remaining consults.
Compare which modules each plan includes.
Choose monthly or yearly and complete secure checkout.
After payment, locked features unlock automatically.

profile.title: Profile
profile.summary: Your professional data and verification status.
profile.tip: Confirm name, license, and contact are correct; verification enables clinical use.
body: Your professional profile supports veterinarian-only access. Keep license and contact details current.
steps: Review your veterinary data and specialty.
Check your professional license status.
Update phone or details if they change.
Go to Membership if you need to change plans.

shortcuts.title: Shortcuts & support
shortcuts.summary: Move faster and get help when you need it.
shortcuts.tip: Ctrl+K opens the command palette. Support chat is at the bottom right.
body: If you get stuck in a module, return to this guide or write to support. Chat covers login, payments, and platform use.
steps: Press Ctrl+K (⌘K on Mac) and type the module name.
In Diagnosis, N may also open a new consult (depending on context).
Open support chat for login, payments, or platform use.
Return to this Help center or the tour whenever you want a refresh.
